catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-riev:
The Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Rievaulx describes the first Cistercian foundation in Yorkshire. Thurston, Archbishop of York, wished for a house of the fervent new order in his diocese, and St. Bernard sent a colony under Abbot William at his invitation.

After some delay Walter Espec became founder and chief benefactor, giving an estate in a wild, lonely valley of the rivulet Rie, ringed by steep hills near Helmsley. The community took possession in 1131, dedicating church and abbey, like all Cistercian houses, to Mary. At first their crude, untilled land left them in want, until Espec's renewed aid and their own incessant labour made it productive.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ernst-von-las:
Ernst von Lasaulx, a scholar and philosopher, was born at Coblenz on 16 March 1805 and died at Munich on 9 May 1861. Bonn was his first university, from 1824 to 1830, and Munich followed for classical philology and philosophy. There he attached himself in particular to Schelling, Görres, and Baader.

Four years of travel through Austria, Italy, Greece, and Palestine followed, visiting civilization's most famous places, pagan and Christian. He sailed to Athens in the suite of Prince Otto of Wittelsbach, elected King of the Hellenes. On his return he took the doctor's degree at Kiel in 1835. The University of Würzburg then appointed him dozent in classical philology, and the university's youth felt his influence deeply. Meanwhile he married Julie Baader, daughter of the Munich philosopher Franz Baader.
